claimed_purpose.text: Vectorize Hindsight: open-source agent-memory service (retain / recall / reflect) that extracts structured facts, entities, and relationships into per-bank PostgreSQL stores—aimed at long-horizon agents and assistants, not a hosted companion SKU.

mechanisms.text: Store: memory banks isolate users/agents; persisted facts/observations, documents/chunks, entities/links, and bank profiles (disposition/mission); SQL/Postgres backend with optional embedded local mode.

Write: retain ingests content (batch/async, tags, document_id upsert/replace); LLM extraction + consolidation pipeline (observations from source facts); supersession via create+delete; issues #4368/#4417 flag dedup and append/replace edge cases.

Retrieve: multi-stage recall (semantic, BM25, temporal, graph, rerank—stages disableable per bank); reflect agent loop for synthesis/opinions; auto-recall hooks can inject before turns; scan is export-only, not recall.
Forget: document delete and memory PATCH invalidate/restore APIs (memories doc); bank wipe/clear_memories; update_mode replace on re-retain—bank-scoped hard deletes, no retrieve-time hide documented.

Isolation & integrations: bank_id (+ tags strict matching); MCP/OpenClaw/coding-agent patterns in docs; Memory Defense can redact/block before store/recall (#4323 field risk); multimodal retain still open (#1801).

ledger.claim: Retain operation persists curated facts — not a raw transcript log — by extracting entities, relationships, and temporal data via LLM then normalizing into canonical indexes
ledger.quote: Behind the scenes, retain uses an LLM to extract key facts, temporal data, entities, and relationships. It passes these through a normalization process to transform extracted data into canonical entities, time series, and search indexes along with metadata.
ledger.locator: Core Concepts > The Three Operations > Retain
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory is curated facts/observations, not a full transcript log; retained facts are consolidated in the background into deduplicated observations with proof counts
ledger.quote: Retained facts don't stay a flat pile. In the background, Hindsight consolidates related facts into observations — deduplicated beliefs the bank has built up over time. Each observation keeps its supporting evidence with exact quotes and a proof count, and is refined rather than overwritten when new evidence arrives
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall is adaptive: four strategies run in parallel and results are ranked and trimmed to fit a token budget, not blindly dumped into context
ledger.quote: The individual results are merged, ordered by relevance using reciprocal rank fusion and a cross-encoder reranking model, then trimmed as needed to fit within the token limit.
ledger.locator: Core Concepts > The Three Operations > Recall
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Mental models act as a scaffold layer: pre-computed standing answers stored as database rows, injected at agent boot without triggering retrieval or LLM calls
ledger.quote: Reading one is a database read — no retrieval, no LLM call — so an agent can boot with a page of settled knowledge instead of rediscovering it every session.
ledger.locator: Core Concepts > Mental Models & Knowledge Pages
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory Defense provides a per-bank forget/block mechanism at write time: PII and secrets are redacted or blocked before reaching storage
ledger.quote: An opt-in, per-bank policy that scans every retain for secrets and PII against 45 patterns and either redacts the match ([REDACTED:github_token]) or blocks the item before it reaches storage.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: LongMemEval benchmark state-of-the-art performance as of January 2026, independently reproduced by Virginia Tech Sanghani Center and The Washington Post
ledger.quote: It has achieved state-of-the-art performance on the LongMemEval benchmark … The benchmark performance data for Hindsight has been independently reproduced by research collaborators at the Virginia Tech Sanghani Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics and The Washington Post.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The canonical causal-link type written by retain is 'caused_by'; legacy types 'causes', 'enables', 'prevents' are read-only for backward compatibility.
ledger.quote:
CANONICAL_CAUSAL_LINK_TYPE = "caused_by"
LEGACY_CAUSAL_LINK_TYPE_NAMES = ("causes", "enables", "prevents")
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Invalidation of a memory unit deletes its causal edges via FK cascade; the edge descriptors are archived in a JSONB column on invalidated_memory_units so a revert can restore them.
ledger.quote: Invalidation moves a fact out of ``memory_units``, so the FK cascade deletes its ``memory_links`` rows — and nothing could recreate a causal edge, which is extraction output rather than derived data. The descriptor is what the archive row stores so revert can rematerialize the edge (#2864).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Causal links carry a numeric weight, defaulting to 1.0.
ledger.quote: DEFAULT_CAUSAL_LINK_WEIGHT = 1.0
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Observations are stored in memory_units table with fact_type='observation', proof_count, source_memory_ids array, and JSONB history
ledger.quote: Observations are stored in memory_units with fact_type='observation' and include: - proof_count: Number of supporting memories - source_memory_ids: Array of memory UUIDs that contribute to this observation - history: JSONB tracking changes over time
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Source facts and observations are distinct memory types; unconsolidated source facts (experience, world) are fetched, processed, then stamped consolidated_at in the same transaction as their derived observations
ledger.quote: The facts this response consumed are marked consolidated in the SAME transaction as the observations that now carry them.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve policy: recall is anchored on raw fact text, retrieves only observations (not source facts), uses embedding + BM25 with round-robin interleave fusion, filtered to the same tag scope via all_strict
ledger.quote: Round-robin interleave fusion (no cross-encoder): consolidation is looking for an existing near-identical observation to merge into. Both the cross-encoder ... and RRF ... were measured to bury that twin; interleave guarantees each retrieval arm's top hits a slot
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget (delete) path: DELETE removes the memory_units row and all observation_history rows for that observation; triggered by LLM DELETE action for superseded or contradicted observations
ledger.quote: Delete a superseded or contradicted observation. ... DELETE FROM {fq_table('memory_units')} WHERE id = $1 AND bank_id = $2 AND fact_type = 'observation' ... DELETE FROM {fq_table('observation_history')} WHERE bank_id = $1 AND observation_id = $2
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Semantic dedup: on CREATE and UPDATE, the new observation is probed against existing observations by cosine similarity; above consolidation_dedup_threshold an LLM adjudicates merge or keep; merge folds sources and deletes the duplicate row
ledger.quote: Semantic dedup: when enabled, an observation that is >= the threshold cosine to a DIFFERENT existing observation is reconciled by a focused 1-by-1 LLM merge (anchored on the observation text, not the source fact). It runs on both CREATE (a near-dup emitted despite the twin being in context — weak-model failure mode) and UPDATE (a rewrite+re-embed that drifts an existing observation into a twin — the create-time guard can't see this).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Observation history is stored per-update in observation_history table as a JSONB pre-update snapshot, trimmed to a configurable max_entries per observation
ledger.quote: Insert one pre-update snapshot into observation_history, then delete the oldest rows beyond max_entries for this observation. The snapshot is stored as a single JSONB content blob (per-row, so it stays small).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is per bank_id and per tag scope; memories with different observation_scopes modes never share an LLM batch; recall uses all_strict tag matching
ledger.quote: SECURITY: Filters by tags using all_strict matching to prevent cross-tenant/cross-user information leakage. Observations are only consolidated within the same tag scope.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Per-scope observation caps: when the cap is reached the prompt instructs the LLM to only UPDATE or DELETE; schema-level maxItems on creates list is also set when supported by the provider
ledger.quote: OBSERVATION LIMIT REACHED ({max_observations_per_scope}/{max_observations_per_scope}). Only UPDATE or DELETE existing observations. Do NOT create new ones — merge new knowledge into existing observations via UPDATE.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Failed consolidation stamps source facts with consolidation_failed_at; this excludes them from the pending-consolidation predicate and is only cleared by explicit bank-wide reset
ledger.quote: that flag is the exclusion predicate for pending consolidation and is cleared only by an explicit bank-wide reset, so a *transient* quota exhaustion permanently orphaned those facts.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Tags are inherited by observations from source facts algorithmically, not by the LLM; on UPDATE, source tags are unioned into the existing observation's tags
ledger.quote: Tags are inherited from the source facts (determined algorithmically, not by LLM) to maintain visibility scope. ... SECURITY: Merge source fact's tags into existing observation tags so all contributors can see it
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Hindsight persists data in a relational database (PostgreSQL or Oracle) via an abstract backend interface with connection pooling.
ledger.quote: Defines the interfaces that all database backends (PostgreSQL, Oracle, etc.) must implement. Business logic depends only on these interfaces.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store supports BM25/tsvector full-text search as a retrieval capability.
ledger.quote: Has BM25 / tsvector full-text search.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store supports partial indexes, relevant to filtered retrieval over persisted rows.
ledger.quote: Can CREATE INDEX … WHERE <predicate>.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store supports delete and update operations (rows-affected normalization is explicitly part of the base interface).
ledger.quote: Execute a DML statement and return the number of rows it affected. Normalizes the dialect-specific execute result into a plain int so callers never hand-parse an "UPDATE <n>" / "DELETE <n>" command tag in business logic
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: An async worker/poller runs against the same database backend, suggesting background jobs operate on persisted data (e.g. extraction, indexing).
ledger.quote: WorkerPoller is backend-agnostic (uses DatabaseBackend.acquire()). All current backends (PostgreSQL, Oracle) support it.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: retain_batch_async is the synchronous write path; it persists a batch of content items (with optional event_date, context, metadata, document_id, tags) into a named memory bank.
ledger.quote:
Retain a batch of memory items.

ledger.quote:
fact_type: If specified, only delete memories of this type.
            delete_bank_profile: If True, also delete the bank profile row itself.
                If False, only delete memories/entities/documents but preserve the bank.

ledger.claim: Memory is isolated per bank_id; all operations are scoped to a bank, and banks are independently listable, configurable, and deletable.
ledger.quote: bank_id: The memory bank ID.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Consolidation is a distinct async process tracked separately from writes; freshness API exposes last_consolidated_at vs last_memory_write_at and pending/failed counts.
ledger.quote:
last_memory_write_at is the newest write
            across the bank's memories — a mental model refreshed at or after it
            cannot be stale, whatever its scope.

ledger.claim: Bank profile persists a 'disposition' (trait dict with int values) and a 'mission' text field; mission supports both full replacement and incremental merge.
ledger.quote: Bank profile dict with bank_id, name, disposition, and mission
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Four retrieval arms exist: semantic (dense vector), BM25 (full-text), graph, and temporal; they return unfused candidates and RRF/rerank happens downstream.
ledger.quote: Returns ``{fact_type: RecallArms(semantic, bm25, graph, temporal)}`` of ``RetrievalResult``: the four per-arm candidate lists, unfused (RRF/rerank happen downstream, unchanged).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memories are typed (fact_type); types include at minimum 'observation', 'world', and 'experience'. Observations are LLM-consolidated summaries of source facts.
ledger.quote: ``pending`` / ``failed`` count the world/experience facts not yet folded into an observation, and those the LLM gave up on.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: updated_at watermark enables incremental export, cache invalidation, and mental-model staleness detection; consolidation scheduler writes exempt themselves from stamping updated_at.
ledger.quote: a write that changes what the memory *is* — text, context, dates, fact_type, tags, metadata, embedding, an observation's sources — stamps ``updated_at``, so a consumer chasing ``WHERE updated_at > watermark`` sees the change.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory isolation is per bank (bank_id); bank storage is created idempotently and can be dropped entirely.
ledger.quote: async def ensure_bank_storage(self, bank_id: str) -> None: """Ensure per-bank storage exists. Idempotent."""
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Scan (scan_memories) is explicitly for browsing and export, not retrieval; it walks the full corpus and is cost O(corpus).
ledger.quote: A full walk by construction — cost grows with the corpus — so this is for browsing and export, never for retrieval.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Concurrent write conflicts are modeled: StoreWriteConflict (stale read-modify-write, must re-read) vs StoreWriteUnavailable (bank mid-migration, retry after 30s).
ledger.quote: A conditional write lost its race: the state it was based on moved before it committed... Distinct from :class:`StoreWriteUnavailable`: that one means "not now, try again shortly" and the same write will succeed unchanged.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Delta re-ingest: replace_chunk_ids scopes replacement to named changed/removed chunks; replace_keep_chunk_ids names survivors as an alternative when changed set is larger.
ledger.quote: ``replace_chunk_ids`` narrows the replace to named chunks of the document — the DELTA case, where every chunk not named keeps its facts.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recency decay is configurable (linear or halflife) with parameters recency_decay_linear_window_days and recency_decay_halflife_days, applied during ranking.
ledger.quote:
recency_decay_function: str = "linear"
    recency_decay_linear_window_days: float = 365.0
    recency_decay_halflife_days: float = 90.0
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: prefer_observations drops raw source facts from results when a returned observation was consolidated from them, backfilling freed slots.
ledger.quote: Drop raw facts that a returned observation was consolidated from, and backfill the freed slots. No-op unless both observations and a raw type were requested.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Facts carry both vector embeddings and a BM25 text_signals field for hybrid retrieval
ledger.quote:
# Build text_signals: entity names + date tokens for enriched BM25 indexing
        signal_parts = []
        if fact.entities:
            signal_parts.extend(e.name for e in fact.entities)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Observations are a consolidated layer derived from source facts (experience, world types); they can be deleted and source facts requeued for re-consolidation independently
ledger.quote: Only the observation rows: requeuing the surviving sources (clearing `consolidated_at`) and resetting the bank's consolidation timestamp belong to the caller, which owns the bank row.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Editing a fact resets consolidation (consolidated_at = NULL) and drops derived links, forcing graph re-maintenance
ledger.quote:
SET text = $3, context = $4, fact_type = $5, occurred_start = $6, occurred_end = $7,
            event_date = $8, consolidated_at = NULL, consolidation_failed_at = NULL,
            edited_at = now(), updated_at = now()
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Embedding and search_vector are excluded from the archive to prevent dimension/type mismatch on model or backend change; embedding is set by the caller after restore
ledger.quote: making a model or text-backend switch structurally unable to trip a type/dimension mismatch (#2209, #2503); each is recomputed on revert.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory units have three fact types: world, experience, observation; and two states: valid, invalidated.
ledger.quote: The response includes each unit's fact_type ( world | experience | observation ), state ( valid | invalidated ), metadata, entities, occurred dates
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Invalidation is a soft-delete: the row moves to a separate archive table, so recall and consolidation exclude it without needing a filter.
ledger.quote: Behind the scenes, invalidating moves the row out of the active memory_units table into a separate archive, so recall and consolidation never need a 'skip invalidated' filter — the rows simply aren't there.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Editing a fact triggers async re-embedding, drops derived observations/links, and re-runs consolidation and the knowledge graph.
ledger.quote: Hindsight re-embeds the fact, drops the observations and links derived from the old version, and re-consolidates, so downstream knowledge reflects the correction. … The PATCH returns as soon as the change is committed; the graph/observation rebuild happens asynchronously right after.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Observations cannot be directly curated; PATCHing one returns 400. They regenerate from underlying source facts.
ledger.quote: Only raw world and experience facts can be curated. Observations are derived — they regenerate from their sources, so you curate the underlying facts, not the observation. A PATCH on an observation returns 400.
ledger.locator: Curation: editing, invalidating & pruning — When to reach for what
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory isolation is at the bank level; endpoints are all scoped to a bank_id.
ledger.quote: GET /v1/default/banks/{bank}/memories/list … GET /v1/default/banks/{bank}/memories/{id}
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Reprocessing a document resets curation of the facts it produced, because the document is the authoritative source.
ledger.quote: reprocessing a document resets curation of the facts it produced (extraction runs fresh from the original text)
ledger.locator: Documents are the source of truth (callout)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Derived observations carry a refresh history showing how they evolved as new source facts arrived.
ledger.quote: For a derived observation, the history endpoint returns how it was refreshed over time as new source facts arrived
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retain persists curated facts and entity relationships (knowledge graph), not a raw conversation log.
ledger.quote: Content is processed, facts are extracted, entities are identified and linked in a knowledge graph
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall uses four parallel strategies — semantic, keyword, graph, and temporal — to select memories into the turn.
ledger.quote: Four search strategies (semantic, keyword, graph, temporal) run in parallel to find relevant memories
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Reflect is a scaffold step: retrieved memories are injected and a disposition-aware response is generated, separating retrieval from generation.
ledger.quote: Retrieved memories are used to generate a disposition-aware response
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory banks are the isolation boundary; disposition and mission are configured at the bank level.
ledger.quote: Memory Banks — Configure disposition and mission
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: retain() is the write path: LLM extracts structured facts (experience vs world), builds entity/temporal/semantic/causal graph, stores into an isolated memory bank
ledger.quote: When you call `retain()`, Hindsight transforms conversations and documents into structured, searchable memories that preserve meaning and context.
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: What Retain Does
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Facts are classified as 'experience' (agent's first-person history) or 'world' (facts about others); speaker context in retain steers this classification
ledger.quote: Every fact is classified by **whose perspective it captures** — the bank's own agent acting, observing, or interacting — its first-person history … or facts about other people, places, things, and events
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: Two Types of Facts
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Observation consolidation runs asynchronously after retain, synthesizing patterns from new facts into the bank's knowledge base
ledger.quote: Observations are consolidated automatically in the background after `retain()` operations complete. This consolidation process synthesizes patterns from new facts into the bank's knowledge base.
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: Two Types of Facts (note)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: recall() uses four parallel retrieval strategies (TEMPR: semantic, BM25, graph, temporal), fused via RRF, reranked by cross-encoder, truncated to token budget
ledger.quote: When you call `recall()`, Hindsight uses multiple search strategies in parallel to find the most relevant memories … Q[Query] --> S[Semantic] … --> RRF[RRF Fusion] … --> CE[Cross-Encoder] … --> R[Results]
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Token budget governs result selection, not top-k count; results are packed by score until max_tokens is exhausted
ledger.quote: Hindsight is built for AI agents, not humans. Traditional search systems return "top-k" results, but agents don't think in terms of result counts—they think in tokens. … Top-ranked memories selected first. Stops when token budget is exhausted.
ledger.locator: File: developer/retrieval.md, section: Token Budget Management
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Temporal retrieval is relevance-first within a time window and spreads selections across time-buckets to avoid density clustering
ledger.quote: Within the window it selects candidates by **semantic relevance to the query** — not by recency — so the most relevant in-window memory is never dropped just because other memories happen to be more recent. It then **spreads the selection across the window's range**
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Two temporal dimensions per memory: event occurrence time and ingestion time; both are used for different query types
ledger.quote: Hindsight tracks **two temporal dimensions**: … When It Happened … When You Learned It … Without this distinction, old information would either be unsearchable by date or treated as irrelevant.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory isolation is per bank_id; tags provide sub-bank visibility scoping for multi-user deployments
ledger.quote: Tags enable visibility scoping—useful when one memory bank serves multiple users but each should only see relevant memories.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Entity resolution uses fuzzy name matching with co-occurrence and temporal proximity; over-merging can occur on large banks; strictness controlled via ENTITY_TRGM_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD and related vars
ledger.quote: The same entity mentioned different ways gets unified through **fuzzy name matching**, reinforced by co-occurrence and temporal proximity … on a bank with a lot of history, a short new name that resembles an existing entity … can be absorbed into it instead of becoming its own entity.
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: Entity Resolution; File: developer/configuration.md, Database Connection Pool
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget-by-exclusion: a retain mission that matches nothing produces zero memories; the document is stored but unreachable by recall/reflect until reprocessed with a wider mission
ledger.quote: content that produces no facts produces no memories at all. The document itself is still stored, but `recall` and `reflect` search memories, so a document with zero memories cannot be found by either.
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: When a mission excludes everything in a document
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Raw source text (chunks) can be retrieved alongside distilled facts via include_chunks=True; this is the log layer vs the curated-memory layer
ledger.quote: Chunks return the raw text that generated each memory—useful when the distilled fact loses important nuance
ledger.locator: File: developer/retrieval.md, section: Expanding Context: Chunks
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recency scoring decays linearly over 365 days (configurable to exponential); temporal proximity boost active only on time-referenced queries; proof-count boost rewards observations backed by more evidence
ledger.quote: recency = clamp(1.0 - days_ago / 365, 0.1, 1.0) … Only active when the query contains a time reference … For observation-type memories, rewards those backed by more evidence using a logarithmic curve
ledger.locator: File: developer/retrieval.md, section: Stage 3: Combined Scoring (Boosts)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall pipeline stages (BM25, graph, temporal, reranking) are individually disableable per bank via configuration; semantic search always runs as baseline
ledger.quote: Turning all four off reduces recall to a single vector query, which is the lowest-latency configuration there is.
ledger.locator: File: developer/configuration.md, section: Recall pipeline stages
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory Defense blocks prompt injection on the write path; partial blocks processed, full blocks return 422
ledger.quote: When Memory Defense is enabled on the target bank and **every** item in the batch is blocked by policy, the request returns 422 with a violation list … Partial-block batches return 200 with the un-blocked items processed
ledger.locator: File: developer/retain.md, section: Memory Defense and Source Provenance
ledger.label: measured
